def lex_smallest_binary_matrix(row_sums, col_sums):
    """Reconstruct the lexicographically smallest 0/1 matrix with given margins.

    Given row_sums (a list of length n) and col_sums (a list of length m),
    find an n-by-m matrix of 0s and 1s whose i-th row contains exactly
    row_sums[i] ones and whose j-th column contains exactly col_sums[j] ones.
    Among all such matrices, return the one whose row-major concatenation
    (row 0, then row 1, ...) is the lexicographically smallest string of
    '0'/'1' characters (with '0' < '1').

    Input domain: 1 <= n, m <= 20, and every entry of row_sums and col_sums
    is an integer with 0 <= value <= 20 (a value may exceed m or n, in which
    case no matrix exists).

    Output: a list of n strings, each of length m over '0'/'1' -- the rows of
    the matrix, top to bottom.  If no matrix satisfies the sums, return the
    empty list [].  The lexicographically smallest valid matrix is unique, so
    no further tie-breaking is needed.

    >>> lex_smallest_binary_matrix([1, 1], [1, 1])
    ['01', '10']
    >>> lex_smallest_binary_matrix([2, 1], [1, 1, 1])
    ['011', '100']
    >>> lex_smallest_binary_matrix([1], [0])
    []
    """
